flags: The company recorded a non-cash impairment charge on an intangible asset in the nine months ended September 30, 2026. It is reflected in SG&A and partly offset higher earnings. The amount is not stated.

The company recorded a non-cash charge of $8 million for the partial settlement of its Canadian pension plan's projected benefit obligation, included in non-operating pension costs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
With its third quarter 2026 results the company raised its full-year 2026 comparable EPS outlook to a range of $14.85 - $15.05.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: Ryder sells outsourced logistics and transportation services across North America. It reports three segments: Fleet Management Solutions (FMS), Supply Chain Solutions (SCS) and Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS).
quotes: Ryder System, Inc. (Ryder) is a leading provider of outsourced logistics and transportation services throughout North America.
Fleet Management Solutions (FMS), which provides full service leasing, commercial rental and vehicle maintenance services

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: SCS provides fully integrated logistics solutions, and DTS provides turnkey dedicated transportation with vehicles, drivers and management support. Dedicated transportation sold as part of an integrated supply chain solution is mostly reported in SCS.
quotes: Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS), which provides turnkey transportation solutions, including dedicated vehicles, professional drivers, management and administrative support

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the segment table is in millions per its heading
business_model.claim: In 2025 SCS was the largest segment by share of consolidated revenue at 43%, ahead of FMS at 38%. Segment revenue was $12,665 in total (table in millions), made up of FMS 5,845, SCS 5,459 and DTS 2,343 less eliminations of (982).
quotes: In 2025, our global FMS business accounted for 38% of our consolidated revenue.
During 2025, our SCS business accounted for 43% of our consolidated revenue

business_model.claim: In FMS the core product is ChoiceLease. It bundles vehicle and maintenance services, and the customer supplies and supervises its own drivers. ChoiceLease was 60% of FMS total revenue in 2025, and commercial rental was 16%.
quotes: Our lease offering provides customers with bundled vehicle and maintenance services while our customers furnish and supervise their own drivers and exercise control over the vehicles.
During 2025, ChoiceLease revenue accounted for 60% of our FMS total revenue.
During 2025, commercial rental revenue accounted for 16% of our FMS total revenue.

business_model.claim: Commercial rental is a transactional, shorter-term FMS product. Ryder also uses it as substitute vehicles for lease customers. Rental depends on Ryder forecasting demand correctly, because it commits to buy vehicles months ahead.
quotes: Although our commercial rental business is transactional in nature, we focus on building long-term relationships with customers to become their preferred source for commercial vehicle rentals.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1; the 12% for transportation management is printed in the same section
business_model.claim: SCS sells logistics services such as distribution management, dedicated transportation, and transportation management and brokerage. In 2025 distribution management and value-added services were about 36% of SCS revenue, dedicated transportation about 28%, and transportation management 12%.
quotes: During 2025, distribution management and value-added services accounted for approximately 36% of our SCS total revenue.
During 2025, approximately 28% of our SCS total revenue was related to dedicated transportation services.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A segment table (dollars in millions)
business_model.claim: SCS revenue in 2025 was split across industry verticals and a pass-through line. Omnichannel retail was $1,299 (table in millions) and subcontracted transportation and fuel was 1,368, out of SCS total revenue of 5,459.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A
business_model.claim: Customers differ by segment. FMS serves small businesses through large enterprises across many industries. SCS accounts are mostly large enterprises. In SCS and DTS the top ten customers in each segment were about one-third of segment revenue in 2025, so customer concentration is a driver.
quotes: Our FMS customers range from small businesses to large enterprises operating in a variety of industries.
In the U.S., SCS customer accounts are mostly large enterprises with complex supply chains.
During 2025, sales to our top ten customers in each of SCS and DTS accounted for approximately one-third of total revenue and operating revenue for each segment.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1A risk factors
business_model.claim: Most revenue is contractual and long-term, so margins depend on the cost and operating assumptions set in the contract. These include volumes, wages, maintenance costs, interest rates and, for ChoiceLease, residual values.
quotes: Substantially all of our SCS and DTS services, as well as our ChoiceLease and SelectCare products offered through FMS, are provided under long-term contractual arrangements with our customers.

business_model.claim: Demand for Ryder's services tracks customers' production and sales of goods and the health of the North American economy. Rental and used vehicle sales are described as the most exposed to economic conditions.
quotes: The transportation industry is highly cyclical and susceptible to trends in economic activity.
Among our services and product offerings, demand for used vehicles, rental and contractual sales are particularly susceptible to changes in economic and market conditions.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A; figures from the 10-Q cash flow and earnings statements, which are in millions
business_model.claim: The main cost of the lease and rental business is owning and maintaining vehicles: depreciation, maintenance, licences, insurance and operating taxes. Vehicle financing interest is reported separately in interest expense. In the nine months to Sep. 30, 2026, depreciation expense was 1,280 (table in millions) and cost of lease and related maintenance and rental was 1,979.
quotes: Cost of lease & related maintenance and rental represents the direct costs related to Lease & related maintenance and rental revenue and are comprised of depreciation of revenue earning equipment, maintenance costs (primarily repair parts and labor), and other costs such as licenses, insurance and operating taxes.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A; figures from the 10-Q income statement, which is in millions
business_model.claim: The services business (SCS, DTS, SelectCare and fleet support) is driven by labor, purchased transportation and fuel costs. In the nine months to Sep. 30, 2026, services revenue was 6,560 (table in millions) against cost of services of 5,596, and management says cost rose slightly more than revenue because of new-business ramp-up costs in SCS.
quotes: Cost of services represents the direct costs related to services revenue and is primarily comprised of salaries and employee-related costs, subcontracted transportation (purchased transportation from third parties), fuel, lease expense, insurance and maintenance costs.

business_model.claim: In FMS, lease and rental gross margin in 2026 has been squeezed by higher maintenance and insurance costs even as contractual revenue grew. Gross margin was 33% for the nine months against 34% a year earlier. In 2025 the margin had risen on ChoiceLease pricing and maintenance cost savings.
quotes: Lease & related maintenance and rental gross margin percentage slightly decreased in the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, due to higher maintenance and insurance costs.
Lease & related maintenance and rental gross margin and gross margin as a percentage of revenue increased primarily due to higher ChoiceLease pricing and maintenance cost-savings initiatives.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A and in the 10-Q MD&A
business_model.claim: Used vehicle sales are a swing factor in earnings. Ryder bears the risk of reselling vehicles below its residual value estimates. Proceeds per unit fell in 2025 and rose in 2026: in the third quarter, tractors were up 19% and trucks up 5%.
quotes: We bear the risk that we will not be able to resell our used vehicles at a price at or above their residual value estimates.
Average proceeds per unit increased in the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q and 10-K MD&A; figures from the 10-Q MD&A table in millions
business_model.claim: Fuel is sold to FMS customers largely as a pass-through, so it inflates revenue but adds little margin. Third-quarter 2026 fuel services revenue was 154 (table in millions) against 107 a year earlier, with fuel gross margin at 6 in both periods.
quotes: Fuel is largely a pass-through to customers for which we realize minimal changes in margin during periods of steady market fuel prices.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q balance sheet and cash flow statement (in millions)
business_model.claim: The business is capital-intensive and funded largely with debt. On Sep. 30, 2026, revenue earning equipment of 8,565 (table in millions) was the largest asset within total assets of 16,170. Long-term debt was 5,537 and short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt was 1,668.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and income statement
business_model.claim: Interest on this debt is a direct cost of the model. Interest expense was 96 in the third quarter of 2026 (table in millions) against 102 a year earlier, and 290 for the nine months. The effective rate was 5.2%, and management attributes the decline to a lower average debt balance.
quotes: Interest expense decreased 6% in the third quarter and decreased 5% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a reduced average debt balance.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release tables (in millions)
business_model.claim: The latest quarter shows the drivers working together. Third-quarter 2026 total revenue was $3,433 (table in millions) against 3,171, and earnings before taxes were $226 against 190. FMS segment earnings were $177 against 146 and rose to 13.2% of operating revenue from 11.4%. SCS earnings were $91 against 86 and DTS $34 against 36.
quotes: EBT and comparable EBT increased in the third quarter primarily due to improved FMS performance.

business_model.claim: Ryder commits real estate and vehicle capital ahead of demand. SCS multi-client warehouses are leased on anticipated customer demand, so lower-than-expected demand leaves excess capacity and weighs on revenue.
quotes: For example, we make real estate commitments to support our SCS multi client warehouse network based on anticipated customer demand to drive the highest level of utilization and revenue per warehouse.

competitive_position.claim: Ryder describes itself as a leading North American provider of outsourced logistics and transportation, and reports three segments: FMS, SCS and DTS.
quotes: Ryder System, Inc. (Ryder) is a leading provider of outsourced logistics and transportation services throughout North America.

competitive_position.claim: FMS has a large installed base: 141,700 ChoiceLease vehicles serving 11,700 customers, run from 789 operating locations. The company says it operates one of the leading full service leasing, commercial rental and contract maintenance businesses in North America.
quotes: FMS operates one of the leading full service leasing, commercial rental and contract maintenance businesses in North America.

competitive_position.claim: SCS has broad reach: 722 customer accounts (excluding brokerage customers) and 319 warehouses across the U.S., Mexico and Canada. Ryder says it can provide port-to-door, end-to-end solutions.
quotes: We offer port‑to‑door solutions that integrate every step of the supply chain, including international inbound flows and cross‑border logistics, fleet and transportation management, warehousing, manufacturing support and multi-channel final delivery.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, citing third-party estimates
competitive_position.claim: The addressable market is mostly not yet outsourced. Of about $1.5 trillion of U.S. logistics spending in Ryder's target markets, $234 billion was outsourced. Of about 11 million U.S. commercial vehicles, 5 million are privately owned by companies and 1 million are leased or rented from third parties like Ryder.
quotes: Logistics spending in the U.S. in the key target markets in which we operate was approximately $1.5 trillion, of which $234 billion was outsourced.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P4; F2 reports the same EPS
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter 2026 results show momentum: diluted EPS from continuing operations was $4.16, up 25%, and total revenue was up 8%, with higher revenue in all three segments.
quotes: Diluted EPS from continuing operations of $4.16, up 25% from prior year

competitive_position.claim: FMS profitability has improved. Pre-tax earnings as a percent of FMS operating revenue were 13.2% in Q3 2026 against 11.4% a year earlier. Management cites lease portfolio quality and early freight-market recovery, and used-vehicle proceeds per unit rose (tractors 19%, trucks 5%).
quotes: In FMS, pre-tax earnings as a percent of operating revenue rose to 13.2%, reflecting our high-quality lease portfolio and early benefits from the freight market recovery.

competitive_position.claim: Contractual demand is cited as a competitive strength: management reports strong contractual growth in FMS and SCS, with sales activity accelerating in FMS and DTS.
quotes: operating revenue growth rates continued to improve, with FMS and SCS generating strong contractual growth

competitive_position.claim: Returns are reported as improving: twelve-month adjusted ROE was 18% against 17% a year earlier. Management raised its full-year 2026 comparable EPS range.
quotes: Comparable EPS (non-GAAP) range raised to $14.85 - $15.05

competitive_position.basis: stated in P6 tables and P4 text
competitive_position.claim: Not all segments are gaining. SCS pre-tax earnings fell 6% over nine months of 2026 ($255 vs $271, table in millions), and DTS operating revenue fell 3% over nine months. Management links DTS to a lower fleet count.
quotes: partially offset by lower DTS fleet count
partially offset by lower SCS results

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2; P5 confirms no material change
competitive_position.claim: Threat: competition may pressure pricing and share. Ryder names rivals with greater capital resources or lower cost structures, new entrants, customers who self-supply, and bidding that depresses rates.
quotes: we compete with many other transportation and logistics service providers, some of which have greater capital resources or lower cost structures than we do
customers may choose to provide the services we provide for themselves

competitive_position.claim: Threat: customer concentration in SCS and DTS. The top ten customers in each segment were about one-third of that segment's revenue, so losing one or more large customers could hurt results.
quotes: During 2025, sales to our top ten customers in each of SCS and DTS accounted for approximately one-third of total revenue and operating revenue for each segment.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: technology change. Warehouse automation has already affected the supply chain business, and zero-emission vehicles could reduce demand for diesel vehicles and related maintenance.
quotes: Advancements in warehouse automation technology, such as autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), have impacted, and may continue to impact, our supply chain business.
Certain innovations, such as an increase in customer use of zero-emission vehicles, for example, could reduce the demand for our diesel vehicle and related maintenance and other offerings.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: used-vehicle and residual-value exposure. In 2025 FMS earnings fell because used truck and tractor pricing dropped 15% and 11%, and Ryder bears the risk of reselling vehicles below its residual estimates.
quotes: We bear the risk that we will not be able to resell our used vehicles at a price at or above their residual value estimates.

competitive_position.basis: figures stated in F1 and P4; competitive linkage stated in P2
competitive_position.claim: Threat: capital intensity and funding cost. Revenue earning equipment (8,565) was a large part of total assets (16,170) (both in millions). Debt to equity was 242%, and Ryder names cost of capital as a significant competitive factor.
quotes: because cost of capital is a significant competitive factor, any increase in either the cost of our debt or equity as a result of, for example, reductions in our debt rating or stock price volatility could have a significant impact on our competitive position

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet and cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Cash is unchanged: cash and cash equivalents were 198 at the latest quarter end and 198 at prior year-end (table in millions). Cash alone is small next to the debt due within a year.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the interpretation is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Current liabilities exceed current assets: total current assets were 2,600 against total current liabilities of 3,882, and current liabilities were 2,778 at prior year-end (table in millions).

financial_health.basis: Balances are stated; the reclassification explanation is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Debt due within a year has roughly doubled: short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt was 1,668, up from 819, while long-term debt fell to 5,537 from 6,826 (table in millions).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the quarterly MD&A, balance sheet and earnings release.
financial_health.claim: Leverage is high but easing: debt to equity was 242% against 250% at prior year-end, and shareholders' equity was 2,977 against 3,052 (table in millions). The full-year outlook gives debt-to-equity of 245%.
quotes: Represents total debt divided by total equity.
Debt-to-Equity | 245%

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement and MD&A.
financial_health.claim: Debt service cost is falling: interest expense was 96 against 102 in the quarter and 290 against 304 for nine months, with an effective rate of 5.2% in each period (income statement in millions).
quotes: Interest expense decreased 6% in the third quarter and decreased 5% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a reduced average debt balance.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and MD&A; the capex attribution is inferred from the statement lines.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash generation is large and rising: net cash from operating activities from continuing operations was 1,985 against 1,845 for nine months. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, was 992 against 496 (statement in millions).

financial_health.basis: Line items are stated; the quality assessment is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Cash generation is largely non-cash depreciation, not net earnings: net earnings were 388 against operating cash flow of 1,985, and depreciation expense was 1,280 (statement in millions).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: Working-capital items drew on cash: receivables used 183 and accrued expenses and other liabilities used 132, partly offset by accounts payable adding 74 (statement in millions).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Cash was returned to shareholders alongside debt reduction: dividends were 113 and share repurchases 372. Net commercial paper repayments were 576, debt proceeds 496 and debt repayments 398, for net financing outflow of 977 (statement in millions).

financial_health.basis: Outlook stated in the earnings release; the implication is inferred.
financial_health.claim: The company's own full-year outlook keeps net operating cash flow at $2.6 billion and free cash flow at $700 million - $800 million, with capital expenditures of $2.4B. Nine-month free cash flow of 992 already exceeds that range.
quotes: Net cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations remains at $2.6 billion and free cash flow (non-GAAP) unchanged at $700 million - $800 million

financial_health.basis: Figures stated; the sources of repayment are inferred from the cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing need and sources: debt due within a year is 1,668 (table in millions). It can be met from operating cash flow of 1,985 and new debt issuance (496 of proceeds in nine months), with commercial paper as a further source. Cash on hand is 198.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
growth_thesis.claim: Fleet Management Solutions (FMS) is the main earnings driver. Its third-quarter pre-tax earnings were $177 against 146 a year earlier (table in millions), and rose to 13.2% of FMS operating revenue from 11.4%. For this to continue, the improvement in lease, rental and used-vehicle results has to hold.
quotes: EBT and comparable EBT increased in the third quarter primarily due to improved FMS performance.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
growth_thesis.claim: Contractual operating revenue growth in Supply Chain Solutions (SCS) and FMS drives the top line. Operating revenue was $2,759 against 2,611 (table in millions), up 6%, with SCS up 9%, FMS up 5% and Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS) down (1)%. Continued growth requires new SCS business to keep ramping and the DTS fleet-count decline to stop dragging.
quotes: operating revenue growth rates continued to improve, with FMS and SCS generating strong contractual growth

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the risk is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Better used-vehicle pricing and mix is a driver. Average proceeds per unit rose 19% for tractors and 5% for trucks in the third quarter. For this to continue, used-vehicle pricing and retail volume have to stay firm, with no repeat of last year's wholesale push to cut aged inventory.
quotes: We also experienced improving trends in used vehicle sales driven by stronger than expected pricing and retail sales volumes, and our rental business has benefited from the execution of our asset management practices.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by the company for EPS; the share counts and repurchase amounts come from the financial statements.
growth_thesis.claim: Share repurchases amplify per-share growth. Shares outstanding fell to 38,218,715 from 39,417,224, and diluted EPS from continuing operations rose 25% against 17% growth in earnings from continuing operations. Continuation requires cash generation to keep funding buybacks (common stock repurchased of (372) against (350), table in millions) alongside capital spending.
quotes: Comparable EPS (a non-GAAP measure) from continuing operations of $4.33, up 21% from prior year, reflects higher earnings in Fleet Management Solutions (FMS) and share repurchases

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and the release; the initiative types are listed in the 10-K.
growth_thesis.claim: Management's strategic initiatives are cited as a driver, with over $70 million of expected earnings benefits this year. Delivery of that figure is what has to hold.
quotes: In addition, we remain on track to deliver over $70 million in expected earnings benefits from strategic initiatives this year, and are well positioned for continued growth.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the financial statements.
growth_thesis.claim: Lower capital spending is lifting free cash flow and easing leverage. Free cash flow was $992 against 496 (table in millions), total capital expenditures were $1,448 against 1,605, and debt to equity was 242% against 250%. This needs operating cash flow to stay strong and capital spending to stay restrained.
quotes: Debt to equity (3) | 242% | 250%

growth_thesis.claim: Lower interest expense supports earnings. Third-quarter interest expense was $96 against 102 (table in millions), at an unchanged effective interest rate of 5.2%. This depends on the average debt balance staying lower.
quotes: Interest expense decreased 6% in the third quarter and decreased 5% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a reduced average debt balance.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management; the cyclicality risk is stated in the 10-K.
growth_thesis.claim: A freight market recovery and strong contractual sales activity underpin future demand, especially for lease and dedicated. Continuation requires that recovery to persist, since the 10-K describes the business as highly cyclical and as slowing before overall market slowdowns.
quotes: Contractual sales activity remained strong across all three segments, with activity accelerating in lease and dedicated.

growth_thesis.claim: Management raised its full-year comparable EPS outlook to $14.85 - $15.05, implying the drivers above are expected to continue. The fourth-quarter comparable EPS outlook is $4.25 - $4.45.
quotes: Comparable EPS (non-GAAP) range raised to $14.85 - $15.05

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the release; the SCS mechanism is partly inferred from the cost-of-services discussion.
growth_thesis.claim: Growth is not uniform across segments. SCS pre-tax earnings for nine months were $255 against 271 (table in millions), down (6)%, which partly offset FMS gains. Growth therefore depends on SCS and DTS returning to their earnings targets.
quotes: partially offset by lower SCS results

quotes: SG&A expenses increased 2% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a non-cash impairment charge related to an intangible asset and higher compensation-related expenses.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item (10-Q MD&A).

quotes: The nine months ended September 30, 2026, includes an $8 million non-cash charge for the partial settlement of our Canadian pension plan’s projected benefit obligation.

quotes: Short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt | 1,668 | 819

quotes: Cost of services increased slightly more than revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to costs incurred to ramp up new business in SCS.

P4.s51.text: Total revenue increased 8% in the third quarter of 2026, and 4% in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, reflecting higher operating revenue and fuel revenue due to higher prices passed through to customers.

unknowns: The filings give no year-to-date operating income, so the year 1 operating margin cannot be tied to 2026 results and stays at the record-neutral level.
The 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $2.4B is stated, but no menu option carries it, so the pooled capex ratio is kept.
Nothing in the evidence shows how revenue growth or margins behave beyond 2026, so years 2 onward stay at the record-neutral options.
The fuel pass-through lifted third-quarter revenue, and how long it lasts is not known.

verdict_reason: expected return -20.0 points a year against the required return over 3 years
